brief: A three-storey cabinet with at least three drawers.

requirements.evidence: Half-n bases stacked at 0,0 levels 0, 1 and 2 (piece:0,0,0;half-n, piece:0,0,1;half-n, piece:0,0,2;half-n) form a three-storey tower 240 mm tall, finished with a top cover (cover:0,0,2;half-n;top) and widened at the base by two full ground cells for stability.
Three classic-style drawers, one on the cut face of each storey: drawer:0#0,0#cut (level 0), drawer:1#0,0#cut (level 1), drawer:2#0,0#cut (level 2).
capOpenFaces applied (16 solid caps on open side faces) and lockJoints applied (joint bolt on the base wall); check_build reports no issues, a single joined group at storey 0, and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: A three-storey cabinet: a tower of three half-n hex bases (levels 0–2, 240 mm tall) standing on a three-cell ground row for stability, with one classic drawer on the cut face of each storey, a half cover on top, all open faces capped solid and the base joints bolted. Three drawers total. check_build is clean with meshClash clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three storeys, three-plus drawers — scouting the current build and drawer options first.

result.note: Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: A drawer needs a half base to sit on, so I'll rebuild the starter cell as a three-high stack of half bases — one drawer per storey.

offersNear.note: Open offers at the base just added (valid until the next change): apply one by its socket, no find_sockets needed.
Open offers at the base just added (valid until the next change): apply one by its socket, no find_sockets needed.

events.text: All three storeys offer drawers — fitting one per level now.
Three classic drawers are in. This is a cabinet, so I'll give it a finished top cover, then run the house rules.
A thin single-column tower wants neighbours, so before capping I'll add two full ground cells beside it; the house rules can lock those joints too.

warnings.message: 1 part(s) could slide apart (1 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.

offersNear.note: Open offers at the base just added (valid until the next change): apply one by its socket, no find_sockets needed.

events.text: House rules done — and capOpenFaces sealed the drawer faces too. I'll check the build, then look at it as you would.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.

events.text: The check is clean (one joined group, no issues, mesh clear) and no props are needed for a cabinet brief — but I want to confirm the cabinet reads as a three-storey tower first.
